name: LME49860 / LME49870
type: Bipolar audio op-amp, ±22 V, dual / single
tagline: The 44 V member of National's LM4562/LME49720 series: 2.7 nV/√Hz, 0.00003% THD+N, ±22 V rails. In Sony PHA-2/PHA-3.

lineage.note: Rev 1.0 06/01/07, rev 1.1 06/11/07. Part of the LM4562/LME49720/LME49710/LME49740 ultra-low-distortion series.
SNAS389C reformat April 2013. LTB 28 Sep 2016 for MA/NA and LME49870; only MAX/NOPB active (Nov 2025).

part_numbers.note: SOIC-8 reel (2500), marking 'L49860 / MA'; .A/.B variants. Mouser 926-LME49860MAX/NOPB.
SOIC-8 tube; LTB 28 Sep 2016 (E2E 456802). Distributor replacement: OPA1612AID.
PDIP-8, the rollers' favourite; LTB 28 Sep 2016. Distributor replacement: OPA2227P (±18 V).
Demonstration boards (SOIC, PDIP) named in SNAS389C; not ICs.
44 V single; LTB 28 Sep 2016. TI literature number unknown; PDIP version unconfirmed.

key_specs.value: 2.7 nV/√Hz typ, 4.7 max; 0.34 µVrms (20 Hz–20 kHz)
55 MHz typ, 45 MHz min; FPBW 10 MHz
±2.5 V to ±22 V (46 V absolute max)
10.2 mA typ (±18 V); 10.5 typ / 13 max mA (±22 V)
±37 mA typ / ±30 mA min (±22 V); text says ±26 mA
10 nA typ / 72 nA max; IOS 11 / 65 nA
Bipolar; Zdiff 30 kΩ, Zcm 1000 MΩ; input clamp diodes

reputation.summary: The ±22 V member of the LM4562/LME49720 series with the same headline numbers. Forums call it refined and detailed with a wide stage; diyAudio a 'very good all-rounder' with slightly 'synthetic' highs. Soomal found it firmer than MUSES02 yet warm. Japanese blogs praise its clarity; some find it plain. Opinion splits on whether it differs from the LME49720.
sonic_descriptors: firmer, more tension (更硬朗，有张力)
typical_uses: DAC output and filter stages (Gustard A18)
Balanced preamps (Gustard P26, now SO-8 on adapter)
Sony PHA-2/PHA-3 and VentureCraft Vantam gain stages
Op-amp rolling; ±22 V line drivers, RIAA preamps, filters
caveats: Isolate capacitive loads above 100 pF with a series resistor; mind socket parasitics and decoupling.
1.6 pA/√Hz current noise erases its voltage-noise edge in ≈20 kΩ networks; use low-impedance feedback.
About 10.5 mA per package at ±22 V: heat and battery drain in portables.
DIP-8 and SOIC tube obsolete since 2016; DIP sockets now need an SO-8 adapter.
Input diodes conduct on large differential input, so not a comparator. Popcorn-noise reports concern LM4562/LME49720.

counterfeit_notes: No specific reports, but NA/NOPB, MA/NOPB and LME49870 are obsolete, so 'new' DIPs are old stock; sibling fakes exist. Genuine SOIC reads 'L49860 / MA'. Check Iq (~10.5 mA), noise and GBW; don't first power suspects at ±22 V.
alternatives: NE5532 (±22 V is its absolute max)

'Changed layout of National Data Sheet to TI format.' No spec changes. Header: JUNE 2007 – REVISED APRIL 2013.
Addendum refresh: only LME49860MAX/NOPB (.A/.B) Active, marking L49860/MA. NA and MA orderables gone after 2016 LTB.

open_questions: What are the LME49870's TI literature number and last revision? Did a PDIP LME49870NA/NOPB exist?
Which TI PCN set the 28 Sep 2016 LTB, and is LME49860MAX/NOPB still active in 2026?
Which National revision do the NSC mirrors hold? Did SNAS389 -, A or B ever exist?
Is it the same die as LME49720 ('a LME49720 that passed a higher voltage test')? Is LME49870 the single version?
What did the head-fi round-up (thread 870832) measure? What op-amp did the LXA-OT1 kit ship with?

refuted_claims: Doubt that LME49870 exists is refuted: alldatasheet (NSC 219107, TI 841155), datasheetcatalog and DigiKey list the 44 V single (https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/219107/NSC/LME49870.html).
Claim that TI 'discontinued the entire 44V LME line' not adopted: the Nov-2025 addendum lists LME49860MAX/NOPB as Active.
corrections: LME49860MA/NOPB and NA/NOPB set to obsolete: DigiKey lists both obsolete; E2E 456802 gives LTB 28 Sep 2016 with LME49710/LME49720 MA/NA.
LME49870 entry renamed LME49870MA/NOPB, confirmed as the 44 V single, obsolete (LTB 28 Sep 2016).
TI product-page datasheet entry raised from low to high confidence.
